plain: Futsal is a variant of soccer played indoors on a smaller, hard court instead of grass, with five players per side (four plus a goalkeeper) instead of eleven, using a smaller, heavier ball with less bounce that encourages close ball control over long passes. Games are shorter, typically two 20-minute halves, and use different rules around boundaries (no throw-ins, since the ball stays in play off walls or is kicked back in) and fouls, with accumulated team fouls leading to penalty-style free kicks. plain: The first modern trading card game was Magic: The Gathering, created by mathematician Richard Garfield and published by Wizards of the Coast in 1993. It introduced the core mechanics that essentially defined the genre: collectible individual cards of varying rarity sold in randomized packs, deck-building from a personal collection, and a rules system built around resource management (mana) and strategic card interactions. It was wildly successful almost immediately and directly inspired the entire trading card game industry that followed, including Pokémon (1996) and Yu-Gi-Oh! (1999). Before Magic, there were sports trading cards and non-game collectible cards, but Magic was the first to combine collectibility with an actual strategic game played between opponents.

plain: Awadhi (Lucknowi) biryani is traditionally mild and aromatic rather than fiery, so making a non-spicy version is actually close to authentic style. Marinate bone-in chicken pieces in yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, a little salt, and warm spices like garam masala, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, and mace for a few hours (skip red chili powder and green chilies entirely). Fry sliced onions until golden and set some aside for layering. Cook the marinated chicken gently until nearly done, then layer it in a heavy pot with 70% cooked basmati rice, fried onions, fried nuts and raisins, saffron milk, mint, and a light drizzle of ghee. Seal the pot tightly (the "dum" method, traditionally with dough around the lid) and cook on very low heat for 20-25 minutes so the flavors and steam finish everything together gently.

plain: The process where matter converts directly from a solid to a gas, skipping the liquid phase entirely, is called sublimation. The reverse process, gas directly to solid, is called deposition.

plain: A refractor telescope uses a glass lens at the front to bend (refract) and focus incoming light, similar to how binoculars work, producing sharp, high-contrast images and requiring little maintenance since there's no exposed mirror to collect dust or need re-aligning. A reflector telescope uses a curved mirror at the back of the tube to gather and focus light instead, which allows for much larger apertures at a lower cost since large mirrors are cheaper to make than equally large lenses, making reflectors generally better for viewing faint, deep-sky objects like galaxies and nebulae. Refractors tend to be better for high-contrast planetary and lunar viewing and are more grab-and-go friendly, while reflectors give you more light-gathering power per dollar but need occasional mirror alignment (collimation) and cleaning.

plain: The easiest visual cue is the snout: alligators have a broad, rounded, U-shaped snout, while crocodiles have a narrower, more V-shaped, pointed one. Another giveaway is the teeth: when an alligator's mouth is closed, its upper jaw is wider than the lower one, so its teeth are mostly hidden; a crocodile's upper and lower jaws are roughly the same width, so its teeth interlock and are visible even with its mouth shut, giving crocodiles that classic toothy grin. Alligators are generally found in freshwater and tolerate cooler temperatures better, mostly in the southeastern US and China, while crocodiles are found more widely across the tropics worldwide and can tolerate saltwater thanks to salt glands, making them more common in coastal and estuarine habitats.
